title: Applications
description: Business applications whose access the platform manages: their permissions, roles and who holds them. They ask the Role Query API what a person may do.

empty.title: No applications registered yet
empty.description: Register an application to manage its roles here and let it ask the Role Query API who may do what.

platform.description: This platform. Its roles and permissions are managed on Roles & access.
platform.title: This is the platform itself.
platform.notice: Its roles are platform roles — create, edit, grant and make them requestable on Roles & access.

card.members: {count, plural, one {person with access} other {people with access}}

copy.failed: Couldn’t copy — select the text and copy it manually.

form.createDescription: Define its permissions and roles next, then grant access or let people request it.
form.editDescription: Changes are recorded in the audit log.
form.name: Name
form.keyHint: The application passes this key to the Role Query API (?application=…). It can’t be changed later.
form.keyLocked: The key can’t be changed — applications use it to call the Role Query API.
form.descriptionPlaceholder: What is the application used for?
form.ownerHint: The person accountable for who has access to this application.

validation.name: Enter a name.
validation.key: Use 2–64 lowercase letters, digits, “-” or “_”, starting with a letter or digit.
validation.keyReserved: This key is reserved for the platform.
validation.keyTaken: An application with this key already exists.
validation.url: Enter a full http(s) address, e.g. https://erp.example.com.

detail.notFound: This application doesn’t exist or was deleted.
detail.notFoundDescription: It may have been removed, or you may not have access to it.

overview.detailsHint: How the application is identified and who is responsible for it.
overview.howHint: The application defines what can be done, roles bundle it, and the platform answers who holds what.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.body: {count, plural, =0 {No permissions yet — list the actions the application checks.} one {# permission the application checks.} other {# permissions the application checks.}}

roles.title: Roles
roles.body: {count, plural, =0 {No roles yet — bundle permissions into roles.} one {# role bundles those permissions.} other {# roles bundle those permissions.}}

access.title: People with access
access.body: {count, plural, =0 {Nobody has access yet.} one {# person holds a role, directly or through a group.} other {# people hold a role, directly or through a group.}}

clients.title: API clients
clients.body: {count, plural, =0 {No API client can query this application yet.} one {# API client can ask the Role Query API about it.} other {# API clients can ask the Role Query API about it.}}

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.description: Deleting the application removes its permissions, its roles and every grant of those roles.
danger.summary: {roles, plural, =0 {No roles} one {# role} other {# roles}} · {members, plural, =0 {nobody with access} one {# person with access} other {# people with access}}
danger.confirmBody: This can’t be undone. It’s recorded in the audit log.
danger.loseRoles: {count, plural, =0 {Its permission catalog is deleted.} one {Its permission catalog and # role are deleted.} other {Its permission catalog and # roles are deleted.}}
danger.loseAccess: {count, plural, =0 {No one currently has access.} one {# person loses access immediately, including grants from approved requests.} other {# people lose access immediately, including grants from approved requests.}}
danger.loseQuery: The Role Query API stops answering for this application, so API clients querying it get “not found”.

permissionPicker.search: Search or type a pattern, e.g. invoices.*
permissionPicker.covers: {count, plural, =0 {matches nothing yet} one {covers # permission} other {covers # permissions}}
permissionPicker.noMatch: No matching permissions. Type a key or a pattern with * to add it.
permissionPicker.emptyCatalog: The catalog is empty. Type a key or a pattern with * to add it.
permissionPicker.typeHint: Wildcards like invoices.* also cover permissions added to the catalog later.

roles.hint: Roles bundle the application’s permissions. Grant them directly, or make them requestable so people can ask for access.
roles.grants: {count, plural, =0 {Not granted} one {# grant} other {# grants}}

empty.title: No roles yet
empty.description: Create a role from the application’s permissions, then grant it or let people request it.

roles.deleteBody: The role is removed permanently and the Role Query API stops returning it. This is recorded in the audit log.
roles.deleteWarning: {count, plural, one {# person or group} other {# people or groups}} will lose this role immediately.

roleForm.createDescription: A role of {app}: a name, the permissions it grants, and whether people can request it.
roleForm.editDescription: Changes take effect immediately for everyone holding the role, and are recorded in the audit log.
roleForm.name: Name
roleForm.keyHint: Returned by the Role Query API. Lowercase letters, digits, “-” and “_”; can’t be changed later.
roleForm.keyLocked: The key can’t be changed — applications may rely on it.
roleForm.permissionsHint: Pick from the catalog, or add a wildcard pattern such as invoices.*.
roleForm.settingsFailed: The role was saved, but its request settings weren’t: {error}

validation.name: Enter a name.
validation.key: Use 2–64 lowercase letters, digits, “-” or “_”, starting with a letter or digit.
validation.keyTaken: This application already has a role with this key.
validation.permissions: One or more permissions aren’t valid keys or patterns.

permissions.title: Permission catalog
permissions.hint: The actions this application checks. Roles grant them by key or by wildcard pattern.
permissions.keyHint: Lowercase segments separated by dots, e.g. invoices.approve (up to 6 segments).
permissions.keyInvalid: Use lowercase segments separated by dots, e.g. invoices.approve.
permissions.keyExists: That permission is already in the catalog.
permissions.removeBody: It’s removed from the catalog. This is recorded in the audit log.
permissions.removeWarning: {count, plural, one {# role grants it.} other {# roles grant it.}} Roles that list it by name keep it; wildcard patterns stop covering it.

empty.title: No permissions yet
empty.description: List the actions the application checks, e.g. invoices.read or payments.release.

access.summary: {members, plural, =0 {Nobody has access} one {# person has access} other {# people have access}} through {grants, plural, one {# grant} other {# grants}} (directly or through groups).
access.label: People with access to {app}

empty.title: Nobody has access yet
empty.description: Grant a role to a person or a group, or make a role requestable.

grant.title: Grant access to {app}
grant.description: Give a person or group one of the application’s roles. Every grant is recorded in the audit log.
grant.maxDurationNote: Requests for this role are limited to {duration}; direct grants aren’t.
grant.scopeGlobal: The role applies everywhere in the application.
grant.scopeDepartment: The role applies only within this department and its sub-departments — the Role Query API reports it as scoped.

query.title: Role Query console
query.hint: See exactly what {app} gets back from the Role Query API for a person.
query.inactive: This person is {status}, so the API returns no roles or permissions.

empty.title: Pick a person
empty.description: Their roles in {app} (with scope, expiry and how they got them) and effective permissions appear here.

check.title: Check a permission
check.hint: Is {name} allowed to do one thing?
check.permissionHint: Pick from the catalog or type any key.
check.departmentHint: Also count roles granted for this department or a parent department.
check.stale: The inputs changed — check again to refresh.

examples.title: Call it yourself
examples.hint: Requests your application makes, using this host.
examples.apiKeyHint: Send an API client’s secret as a bearer token. The client must be allowed to query this application.
examples.oauthHint: Or exchange the client ID and secret for a one-hour access token, then use it as the bearer token.
examples.members: Everyone with a role (for provisioning sync)

clients.title: API clients
clients.description: Service accounts that other systems use to call the platform — usually to ask the Role Query API what a person may do in an application.

empty.title: No API clients yet
empty.description: Create a client for each system that needs to ask who may do what.

forbidden.title: You can’t manage API clients
forbidden.description: Ask a platform administrator for access.

form.createDescription: Its secret is shown once, right after you create it.
form.editDescription: Change what the client can reach. Changes are recorded in the audit log.
form.tokensRevoked: Saving revokes the client’s outstanding OAuth access tokens — it must request a new one. API keys keep working.
form.name: Name
form.descriptionPlaceholder: Which system uses it, and for what?
form.allAppsHint: It can query every application, including ones registered later.
form.selectedHint: It can ask the Role Query API about these applications only.
form.permissionsHint: Optional. Lets the client call other platform APIs, e.g. core.users.read. You can only give permissions you hold.
form.notHeld: You can’t give permissions you don’t hold yourself: {permissions}
form.cidrsHint: Optional. Only requests from these addresses are accepted, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8. Leave empty to allow any address.
form.cidrInvalid: Enter an IP address or CIDR range, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8.
form.daysInvalid: Enter a whole number of days from 1 to 730.
form.expiryHint: Add a new secret before it expires to rotate without downtime.
form.neverHint: Secrets that never expire are riskier — rotate them regularly.

validation.name: Enter a name.
validation.reach: Choose at least one application, or give it platform permissions under Advanced.

reveal.title: “{name}” is ready
reveal.description: Give the secret to the system that will use this client.
reveal.rotatedDescription: Deploy it, then revoke the old secret once nothing uses it.
reveal.warning: You won’t be able to see it again — only a fingerprint is stored. If it’s lost, add a new secret.
reveal.stored: I’ve stored the secret somewhere safe

examples.apiKeyHint: Ask what {user} may do, with the secret as a bearer token.
examples.apiKeyHintNoApps: Send the secret as a bearer token. This client can’t query any application yet.
examples.oauthHint: Exchange the client ID and secret for a one-hour access token (client credentials).

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.hint: A client can hold several secrets, so you can rotate without downtime: add a new one, deploy it, then revoke the old one.
secrets.addDescription: The new secret works alongside the existing ones. It’s shown once.
secrets.revokeBody: Requests using this secret stop working immediately, and the client’s OAuth access tokens are revoked.
secrets.revokeLastBody: This is the client’s last active secret — it can’t authenticate until you add a new one. Its OAuth access tokens are revoked too.

detail.reachHint: What the client can ask about, and from where.
detail.examplesHint: Use one of the client’s secrets in place of the placeholder.
detail.dangerHint: Revoking the client disables all its secrets and access tokens. It can’t be undone.
detail.revokeBody: Every secret and access token stops working immediately. The client is kept for the audit trail but can’t be changed or used again.
detail.revokedNotice: It can’t authenticate or be changed. Create a new client if the system still needs access.
